annotations.title: Get crisis help: the real emergency number and crisis line for a country

description: PURPOSE: Give the real emergency number and crisis hotlines (suicide or crisis line, text line, domestic violence, child help) for one country, from the verified dataset The Living Bread ships for 53 countries, with its source and the date it was checked. WHEN TO USE: FIRST, before any other tool, whenever a person speaks of harming themselves or someone else, or is in danger ("I want to die", "my friend is suicidal", "he hits me"). WHEN NOT: for loneliness or a wish to talk with no danger, use find_people_to_pray_with (mode a_person_now); for comfort from the Word afterwards, find_scripture_for. Never give a verse in place of a phone number. PARAMETERS: country is the person's country as a name or ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code ("Nigeria", "GB", "USA"). If you do not know it, ask; this tool never defaults to one country's number. Omit it only to get the list of countries held. OUTPUT: country {code, name} or null; emergency numbers; crisis_line, text_line, domestic_violence and child_help (each name and number, or null); source, verified_at, confidence; rule (how to use the answer); door (the app's crisis page); countries_held when no country matched. BEHAVIOR: read only; a static dataset, no network call. Matching is strict (ISO code, exact name, known alias, or an unambiguous name start of four letters or more) because a wrong line is worse than none. An unheld country returns country null with the general emergency rule (112, 911, 999) and the countries held, never a guessed number. Access: no sign-in; shared limit of 300 requests a minute per IP.

country.description: The person's country: name or ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code ("Nigeria", "GB", "Brazil", "USA"). Omit only to list the countries held.

name: get_crisis_help

answered_by.description: The implementation that answered (the same tool name the signed-in endpoint lists).

attribution.description: Credit line for the data: The Living Bread (living-bread.org).

content_layers.description: Which fields are Scripture and which are human interpretation or reflection.

evidence.description: Present when Scripture was read: translation, canon, corpus version, attribution, and a SHA-256 per passage.

freshness.description: How current the answer is: kind (scheduled | recently_observed | verified_live | record), retrieved_at, available_now (true only when activity was verified live).

ids.description: Up to 25 ids found in this answer, for follow-up calls.

ignored_params.description: Parameters given that this mode does not use.

license.description: License URL of the returned data (CC BY 4.0 unless stated).

next_actions.description: Up to 4 links the person can open next.

ok.description: Always true on a successful answer (errors come back as isError, never here).

result_state.description: "empty" when nothing matched (count 0, no results); the text then says so plainly.

source_url.description: The first public web page this answer came from or points to.

visibility.description: "public" for shared data, "yours" for the signed-in believer's own data.
